speaker_role: current admissions officer (two UH Manoa admissions counselors)
commercial_incentive: None evident (official university enrollment webinar for already-accepted students)
key_insights: This is a post-acceptance enrollment logistics webinar (housing, financial aid, scholarships, registration) for UH Manoa, not general admissions strategy.
Explains the new 'Warrior Scholarship' uses a weighted GPA (factoring AP/IB) with a minimum 3.8 weighted GPA requirement for eligibility.
States the STAR scholarship database offers roughly $9.5 million annually but only about half is typically awarded because students under-apply, so proactive searching pays off.
Explains the Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) program cuts non-resident tuition by nearly half (cited as roughly $33k to $17k/year) for eligible western-state residents, applicable to all majors.
Notes financial aid and scholarships are processed on a first-come, first-served basis tied to submission date, so early FAFSA/STAR submission matters even with a stated priority deadline.
States admissions counselors handle application status questions while separate major-specific academic advisors handle course/major questions.
Notes students can change their declared major via email to admissions up until about mid-April before enrollment; after that, changes go through an academic advisor.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speakers: New Warrior Scholarship deadline January 15; FAFSA priority deadline February 1; STAR scholarship database deadline February 15; UH System scholarship deadline March 1
Speakers: weighted GPA minimum of 3.8 required for New Warrior Scholarships
Speakers: STAR database scholarships total roughly $9.5 million annually, with about half going unclaimed each year
Speakers: WUE tuition reduction brings cost from about $33,000/year to about $17,000/year for eligible non-resident students
Speakers: application processing/decision wait time cited as approximately 8-10 weeks
notable_or_distinctive: Entirely specific to University of Hawaii at Manoa's own enrollment process (scholarships, housing, COVID-era policies) rather than general admissions advice applicable elsewhere.
reliability_notes: This is a live Q&A webinar recorded during the COVID-19 pandemic (early 2021 per content, single-occupancy housing, test-optional policy), so procedural and policy details (deadlines, GPA thresholds, tuition figures, COVID housing rules) are likely outdated and specific to that admissions cycle only.
